title: Two Huangs Don’t Make A Right
gist: Teaser only (paywalled remainder) of a Louis-Vincent Gave piece: he frames recurring US actions just before high-level US-China meetings — the Feb-2023 'spy balloon' that cancelled Blinken's Beijing visit, and the Commerce Department expanding the sanctioned Chinese entity list from 1,500 to 20,000 firms days before the Trump-Xi Busan summit — as a pattern of pre-summit sabotage of détente.

insights.claim: Gavekal's Louis-Vincent Gave highlights a recurring pattern in which US-China diplomatic openings are derailed by a sudden security escalation shortly before a scheduled high-level meeting.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat scheduled US-China summits as event risk with a skew toward last-minute escalation, not as reliable de-escalation catalysts.
insights.locator: I am old enough to remember

insights.claim: In February 2023, a US media frenzy over a Chinese surveillance balloon led to the cancellation of Secretary of State Antony Blinken's inaugural Beijing visit, even though China already has an estimated 1,687 satellites in space.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Illustrates how low-substance security incidents can override diplomatic calendars and move China-sensitive assets.
insights.quote: China already has an estimated 1,687 satellites in space
insights.locator: I am old enough to remember

insights.claim: A few days before the Trump-Xi summit in Busan, South Korea, the US Commerce Department expanded its sanctions entity list, lifting the number of sanctioned Chinese firms from 1,500 to 20,000.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A >10x expansion of the entity list sharply widens compliance exposure for any firm with Chinese counterparties; watch for similar pre-summit actions.
insights.quote: pushed the number of sanctioned Chinese firms from 1,500 to 20,000
insights.locator: A couple of years later, Donald Trump
